intro: Chrome for sales development representatives on Mac is mostly tab management. Your CRM, LinkedIn, inbox, and calendar each need a tab, and you switch between them all day. This guide covers the Chrome features that matter for the job, plus how Lazur helps by voice while you work in the browser.
tldr: Put each account in its own tab group, named for the company.
Press ⌘⌥N on Mac to start split view from the active tab. Back and the address bar only work on the active side.
Use separate Chrome profiles for work and personal accounts so logins and history stay apart.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur where a button is. It circles the button and labels it. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: What your Chrome day looks like as an SDR

An SDR day in Chrome moves between a small set of pages. You open a CRM record, a LinkedIn profile, a sequence tool or inbox, a calendar, and a prospect list in a spreadsheet. Each one needs its own tab. By mid-morning, the window can look like a mess. That is normal, and it is fixable.

The real work is switching. You read a name, check the company, copy a line, paste it into an email, then log the call. Each switch is small. Together they fill the day. Chrome setup matters more for this job than for most browsing, because the switching never stops.

Use the industry research with care. The Bridge Group tracks SDR performance and metrics. It does not study which tabs reps keep open. The tips below come from how the browser works, not from a survey of SDR habits. Treat them as a starting point and test them on your own accounts.
Set up Chrome on Mac before your first call

Start with profiles. Click your profile icon in the top right of the Chrome toolbar and add a profile for work. Sign in with your work Google account there, and nowhere else. Keep personal mail, shopping, and family accounts in a different profile.

Next, show the bookmarks bar with ⌘⇧B. Keep the sites you open every hour there, such as your CRM, your calendar, and your prospect sheet. A bookmark click beats a search. It also keeps working when a page title changes.

Then look at vertical tabs. Google's Chrome page promotes them alongside labeled, colored tab groups. Vertical tabs keep long lists readable on a wide screen. Try them for a full week before you decide. Switching layouts in the middle of a campaign costs more than it saves.

items: Create a work profile and sign in only there.
Right-click your CRM and inbox tabs, then choose Pin. They stay open when Chrome restarts.
Show the bookmarks bar with ⌘⇧B so your daily sites are one click away.
Store work passwords in Google Password Manager, not in notes or a shared sheet.
Open Chrome > About Google Chrome once a month to check for updates.

blocks.text: Tab groups for each account on your list

A tab group is a set of tabs with a name and a color. Right-click a tab, choose Add tab to group, then New group. Type the account name and pick a color. Many SDRs use one color for new prospects, one for follow-ups, and one for accounts that replied.

Here is a worked example with a made-up account called Northwind Tools. You open a group named Northwind Tools. Inside it you put the company website, its LinkedIn company page, the CRM record, and the email thread. You work the account from that group. When the call is logged, you close the group.

Closing a group closes its tabs. Log your notes first. If you close a group by mistake, press ⌘⇧T right away. It brings back the last closed tab, and you press it again for the next one. Act fast, because the list of closed tabs is limited.
The common mistake is one giant group for the whole week. It turns into a second tab bar. Keep groups small. Name them for the work, not for the day.
Split view: your CRM on one side, LinkedIn on the other
Split view puts two tabs side by side in one Chrome window. Press ⌘⌥N to open split view from the active tab. You can also right-click an inactive tab and choose New split view with current tab.

You can drag a tab toward the left, right, or bottom edge of the window. Keep dragging until Create split view appears, then let go. For links, right-click the link and choose Open link in split view. That is handy when a company page comes up from a CRM note.

Split view suits one common pair. Put the CRM record on the left and the company site on the right. Read, type the note, and switch sides without opening a new window. Keep the prospect sheet in a tab group, not in split view, so the layout stays clean.

blocks.title: Split view limits
blocks.text: Back, forward, home, and the address bar only work on the active side. Reading mode collapses when you switch sides. Click the side you want before you use those controls.

Drag-and-drop into split view is on by default. If you drop tabs by accident, turn it off in Chrome > Settings > Appearance. Google's split view help page does not mention tab groups or profiles, so test those on a practice account first.
Keyboard shortcuts for Chrome on Mac

Shortcuts save more time than most settings. These are standard Chrome shortcuts on macOS. Learn a handful first, then add more. Mac shortcuts use ⌘ for Command, ⌥ for Option, ⌃ for Control, and ⇧ for Shift.

rows: Open a fresh search or a prospect page
Recover a CRM page you closed by mistake
Type a company domain without reaching for the mouse
Locate a job title or a phone number
Move down your list of accounts
Go back to the last account
Put the CRM beside the company site
Save a research page for later
Find a page you opened earlier

blocks.text: Press ⌘ with a number key to jump to a tab by its position. Put your CRM in the first spot. Put your inbox in the second. The same order every day builds muscle memory, and muscle memory is faster than looking.
Where SDR time goes, and what the numbers say

Vendor research puts much of an SDR's time into admin. Mixmax, a sales software vendor, cites a DocuSign figure that reps sell about 28% of their time and spend the rest on other tasks. It also cites a Forrester study that the average rep wastes about 14 hours a week on admin.

Those figures come from a vendor blog. The page gives no publication year, and its numbers rest on secondary sources. Treat them as a reason to look at your own week, not as a fact about you. Track one week of tabs and tasks before you change anything.
What the Bridge Group found about SDRs in 2025

The Bridge Group's 2025 SDR report covers 351 B2B companies. It finds that 60% of SDRs are at quota. The report calls that the lowest level in the study's history. The same report puts median SDR annual turnover at 40%, using 2024 data, with a middle range from 21% to 57%.

Average SDR tenure is 1.9 years in 2025. The report describes that as the highest since the early 2010s. Many SDRs are new to their jobs and their tools. Written Chrome habits help a new hire ramp faster than a verbal walkthrough.
Worth saying plainly: the report measures people, pay, and targets. It does not measure browser habits. Use it to understand the job, not to score your tabs.
Ask Lazur about the page you are on
Hold ⌥⌘, Option and Command together, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur sees your screen, answers out loud, and points at things. It listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut.

Good questions for a prospecting tab include these. What does this company sell? Which team does this person run? Where is the contact form? Lazur answers from what is on screen. Check the answer against the page before you use it in an email.

Ask where something is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. That helps when a CRM tucks its log call button under a menu. Lazur does not click it for you. You make the click.
Guided steps for Chrome features you use now and then

Ask how to do something and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. This suits split view and tab group setup, especially when you have not done it before.

Here is an example. You want a group for a new account. Ask, Walk me through making a tab group for this account. Lazur tells you to right-click the tab, then points to Add tab to group, then New group. You name the group and pick a color. Each step waits for your click.

Use guided steps for settings, too. Ask Lazur where drag-and-drop into split view is controlled. It circles the setting and labels it. You change the setting yourself, so you know exactly what changed.
Dictate follow-up emails without leaving Chrome

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. That works in a Gmail compose window, a CRM note, or a LinkedIn message box. The text lands where your cursor sits, so you stay in the tab you are working in.

Snippets save the lines you repeat. Save your calendar link as a snippet, and it is one phrase away. A personal dictionary helps with company names and product terms that voice tools tend to miss. Clipboard slots hold the lines you copy often.

Read dictated text before you send. A name or a time can come out wrong. Check the prospect's name, the company, and the proposed time every time. Dictation is fast, and a fast mistake still reaches the prospect's inbox. If you want to test your own dictation, try the [dictation accuracy checker](/tools/dictation-accuracy-checker).
Research a prospect without losing your place

Research tabs pile up fast. Here is a simple method. Open a tab group for the account. Add the company website, its LinkedIn company page, and a recent news search. Use split view to read the CRM record beside the page you need. Close the group when the call is logged.

Ask Lazur to do the reading in the background. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It does not use the tabs you have open. It comes back with a summary and a report.
Read the report for facts before you put them in an email. A summary is a starting point. Check the company's own page for anything you plan to quote to a prospect.
Keep work and personal browsing apart

Profiles keep cookies, logins, bookmarks, and history separate. Use your work profile for prospect accounts. Use another profile for personal mail and shopping. This stops a personal login from appearing on a client call, and it keeps your work history clean.
Watch for the wrong profile. A new window can open in a different profile than you expect. Check the profile icon in the top right before you type a message. A sent email cannot be unsent.

blocks.title: Quick check
blocks.text: Click your profile icon in the top right before you send anything. The profile name shows which Google account you are using right now.
Google's help page does not say how profiles interact with split view or tab groups. Test split view in your work profile on a spare account before you rely on it during a live call.
Privacy: what Lazur sees and where it goes

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. When you ask a question, the audio and a screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. Those copies are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
A prospect's data still needs care. Check your company's policy before you paste customer details into any AI tool. Close sensitive tabs while you ask a question, so they stay out of the picture.

Scraping is a separate question. Some Chrome extensions pull contact data from LinkedIn. Read the tool's terms, and your company's rules, before you install one. Being listed in the Chrome Web Store does not mean your team approves it.
Mistakes SDRs make with Chrome on Mac
Most problems come from a few habits. These are the ones that cost the most time.

items: One tab group for the whole week. Keep groups small and named for each account.
Working in the wrong profile and sending from a personal account.
Dropping tabs into split view by accident. Turn off drag-and-drop in Chrome > Settings > Appearance if it keeps happening.
Trusting a summary without checking the page it came from.
Keeping every tab open. Log the notes in the CRM, then close the account group.
Pressing back in split view and wondering why the other side did not move. Click the side first.

blocks.text: Edge cases to test on your own Mac

Chrome updates often, so check your version. Open Chrome > About Google Chrome. WhatIsMyBrowser lists 156.0.8078.82 as the latest Chrome build for macOS, dated 2026-11-04. Your build may be newer or older. Match it against what your team uses.

Some behavior is undocumented. Google's split view page says tab-specific features work only on the active view. It does not say how a tab group that holds a split view behaves. Test that on a spare account before you depend on it.

Check your screen setup, too. Try split view on the display you use for calls. A laptop screen and an external monitor give different room for two tabs. Set the window size before a live call, not during one.
A day in Chrome, step by step
Here is a workday that uses the pieces above in order. Change the steps to fit your team and your CRM.

items: Open your work profile and check the profile icon in the top right.
Open a tab group for each account on today's list.
Use split view to put the CRM record beside the company site.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask Lazur what the company does, if you need a fast read.
Hold fn and dictate the follow-up. Read it before you send.
Log the call notes in the CRM, then close the account group.

blocks.text: Where to start this week
Pick one habit to start. Tab groups for each account is the easiest one to begin with. Add split view once the groups feel natural. Add voice help when you have a specific task for it.
When you are ready, check the [pricing page](/pricing) for plans. The [download page](/download) has the Mac app. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available yet.

If your follow-ups go through Gmail, you can schedule them too. Read how to [schedule an email in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail). For prospect sheets, see how to [sort data by column in Google Sheets on Mac](/how-to/sort-data-by-column-in-google-sheets).

faq.question: Is Chrome for sales development representatives on Mac different from Chrome on Windows?
faq.answer: The core features match. You get tab groups, split view, profiles, and shortcuts on both systems. Mac keys differ, so ⌘ replaces Ctrl for most shortcuts. Lazur runs on Mac today. Windows is planned, not available yet.

faq.question: How do I open split view in Chrome on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘⌥N from the tab you want on the active side. You can also drag a tab to the left, right, or bottom edge until Create split view appears. Google's help page lists every route.

faq.question: Why does the back button only affect one side of split view?
faq.answer: Google's help page says back, forward, home, and the address bar work only on the active view. Click the side you want first, then use the controls.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in my CRM for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It points at things, guides you one click at a time, answers questions, and types text when you dictate.

faq.question: What is typical SDR turnover?
faq.answer: The Bridge Group's 2025 report gives median SDR annual turnover of 40%, using 2024 data. Its middle range runs from 21% to 57%. The report ties that figure to a stabilizing labor market.

faq.question: Do I need Lazur to use these Chrome tips?
faq.answer: No. Tab groups, split view, profiles, and shortcuts are Chrome features. Lazur adds voice help on top. Check the pricing page for current plans and trial details.

faq.question: How do I check my Chrome version on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Chrome > About Google Chrome. WhatIsMyBrowser lists 156.0.8078.82 as the latest macOS build, dated 2026-11-04. Compare your build to that before you change settings.
